shots.composition_notes: Locked-off medium two-shot in a garage; the woman (arms crossed, brown sweater) is placed left-of-center and the man (glasses, dark coat) right-of-center, both roughly on the vertical thirds with the gap between them near frame center. Consistent headroom with the garage shelving line running just above their heads; open garage door and blurred house exterior fill the left edge, giving depth without pulling focus. Camera and framing do not change at all across the full ~14.7s scene - only captions (one word/phrase at a time, lower-third) and the characters' micro-expressions change between periodic samples, confirming this is a single static hold rather than multiple shots disguised as one scene.

Same garage two-shot composition as the preceding shot but the image is dimmed/darkened under a title card overlay ("LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / CREATED BY NIN.") - a brief cross-fade transition frame rather than a new camera setup.

Full black end card, no live-action/animated frame visible. Title and creator credit centered horizontally in the upper-middle of frame; a torn-paper "NEW EPISODE DAILY" tag sits centered below with small burst/sparkle marks flanking it, all stacked on the vertical center axis.

framing_patterns_notes: The entire narrative portion of this reel is carried by one unmoving, symmetrical garage two-shot - no cuts, pans, zooms, or coverage changes happen while dialogue plays; all comedic/emotional beats are delivered through captioned dialogue and the characters' facial micro-expressions rather than camera work. The video closes on a static black end card with centered title/credit/CTA text, mirroring the same centered, symmetrical placement logic used in the live scene's two-shot.
